current_reader_summary: The current full reread makes the training choice concrete: the question is visible context, while the separate aligned target sequence decides which next-item predictions count toward the cost. In the short Q/A conversation the assistant boundary predicts A and A predicts the ending, so six input positions have only two scored targets. The new text names input/next-target alignment and the new figure labels Y as next-item targets; neither requires a novice to infer a direction from a shift name. Real image/text training must use the base model’s processor/template and preserve answer/end targets under truncation. The larger counts are clearly counts of encoded scored positions. The A-to-AB exercise is predictable and checkable. Reading §§20.6–20.8 connects this target choice to the trainable correction and the later acceptance decision. I found no current readability blocker.

context_reader_summaries.20.8: The following section distinguishes evidence that chosen weights actually changed from evidence that a resulting version answers unseen questions usefully. It compares saved candidates with the base on the same validation questions, and explains that photo improvements do not compensate automatically for failed chat-retention/end-of-answer conditions. This gives a clear purpose to §20.7’s final transition from choosing scored targets to checking update and delivery decisions. I did not inspect its linked experiments or judge its factual results.
